# A root component's declarations are hoisted into the window it lifts, because
# that is where they are mounted (#215). Two windows is two answers and the
# author is asked, the way a body rendering two families is asked to name one:
# aliasing the var into both emits the field twice, and copying it turns one
# binding into two cells that diverge in silence -- and which of those is wrong
# depends on the target, since two html windows are two pages with their own
# state while two fyne windows share one Model.
#
# The position is the declaration that has nowhere to go, not the component
# header, because that is the line the author has to move.

! sngl generate --lang none --platform html -o out two.sngl
stderr 'two.sngl:10:5: component main declares state and renders 2 windows'
stderr 'declare it in the window that uses it'

# One window is the ordinary case and is not refused.
sngl generate --lang none --platform html -o out1 one.sngl
exists out1/index.html

# Neither is a component that renders two windows and declares nothing: the
# rule is about a declaration with nowhere to go, not about window count.
sngl generate --lang none --platform html -o out2 bare.sngl
exists out2/index.html

-- two.sngl --
import ui "sngl:ui"

output {
    none {
        html
    }
}

component main ui.root {
    var hits = 0

    ui.window #a(title="a", href="/") {
        ui.text(value="{hits}")
    }

    ui.window #b(title="b", href="/b.html") {
        ui.text(value="{hits}")
    }
}
-- one.sngl --
import ui "sngl:ui"

output {
    none {
        html
    }
}

component main ui.root {
    var hits = 0

    ui.window #a(title="a", href="/") {
        ui.text(value="{hits}")
    }
}
-- bare.sngl --
import ui "sngl:ui"

output {
    none {
        html
    }
}

component main ui.root {
    ui.window #a(title="a", href="/") {
        ui.text(value="x")
    }

    ui.window #b(title="b", href="/b.html") {
        ui.text(value="y")
    }
}
